name: Tree Pruning
description: t+pazolite, ginkiha, Hommarju - Paved Garden ⠀ You are given a tree with $$$n$$$ nodes, rooted at node $$$1$$$. In this problem, a leaf is a non-root node with degree $$$1$$$. In one operation, you can remove a leaf and the edge adjacent to it (possibly, new leaves appear). What is the minimum number of operations that you have to perform to get a tree, also rooted at node $$$1$$$, where all the leaves are at the same distance from the root?
input_specification: Each test contains multiple test cases. The first line contains the number of test cases $$$t$$$ ($$$1 \le t \le 10^4$$$). The description of the test cases follows. The first line of each test case contains a single integer $$$n$$$ ($$$3 \leq n \leq 5 \cdot 10^5$$$) — the number of nodes. Each of the next $$$n-1$$$ lines contains two integers $$$u$$$, $$$v$$$ ($$$1 \leq u, v \leq n$$$, $$$u \neq v$$$), describing an edge that connects $$$u$$$ and $$$v$$$. It is guaranteed that the given edges form a tree. It is guaranteed that the sum of $$$n$$$ over all test cases does not exceed $$$5 \cdot 10^5$$$.
output_specification: For each test case, output a single integer: the minimum number of operations needed to achieve your goal.
approach_summary: Precompute 2^k ancestor jumps up[u][k] and node depths in O(N log N). Compute LCA and path aggregates in O(log N) per query.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 2018C — Tree Pruning [146. Binary Lifting and LCA]
topic_editorial.summary: Binary lifting for lowest common ancestor and tree jumps.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: Any ancestor jump of distance $K$ can be decomposed into powers of two $K = \sum 2^j$. Precomputing `up[u][k]` (the $2^k$-th ancestor of $u$) via `up[u][k] = up[up[u][k-1]][k-1]` allows any path or LCA to be answered in $O(\log N)$.
